input.summary: This looks like a one-off transient failure, and no action is needed. The ingest_orders task for 2026-10-28 timed out on its first attempt ("timed out reading landing/orders/2026-10-28.csv after 30s") and succeeded when it was retried automatically. The retry loaded a normal amount of data: 289 rows into raw.orders (the previous 7 days ranged from 253 to 375) and 739 rows into raw.order_items (597 to 968). The 289 rows for 2026-10-28 have 289 distinct order_ids, so the retry did not load anything twice. In the 7-day run history, this is the only attempt that didn't succeed first time, so there is no recurring pattern. The general on-call runbook says to treat this as noise and close it, and to open a ticket only if the task retries on 3 or more days in a week. I'm not proposing any action and have low confidence in any specific root cause; the most likely explanation is a brief network or storage blip while reading the landing file. I saw no instruction-like text in the tool outputs.

evidence.excerpt: If it did, close as resolved; no remediation is needed. Report low confidence in any root cause.

hypotheses_considered: Transient network/storage timeout reading the landing file (healed on retry) - most likely
Late upstream file causing a partial load - rejected: 2026-10-28 row counts are within the normal range
Duplicate load from the retry - rejected: 289 rows and 289 distinct order_ids
Recurring or worsening source problem - rejected: only one retry in the 7-day history
